title: DSA - Polynomial Time
description:
## What is Polynomial Time?
An algorithm runs in polynomial time if its time complexity is O(n^k) for some constant k.

### Polynomial (in P):
| Complexity | Example |
|---|---|
| O(1) | Array index access |
| O(log n) | Binary search |
| O(n) | Linear search |
| O(n log n) | Merge sort |
| O(n²) | Bubble sort |
| O(n³) | Matrix multiplication (naive) |

All of these are n raised to some fixed power. Even O(n^100) is polynomial (though impractical).

### NOT Polynomial (exponential/factorial):
| Complexity | Example |
|---|---|
| O(2^n) | Brute force subset generation |
| O(n!) | Brute force permutations |
| O(n^n) | ... don't |

The gap between polynomial and exponential is MASSIVE:
- n = 100, O(n²) = 10,000 operations
- n = 100, O(2^n) = 1,267,650,600,228,229,401,496,703,205,376 operations

That's why P vs NP matters. If a problem has no known polynomial solution, it's essentially unsolvable for large inputs.
